candidates.title: Bodyweight vs Weighted Pull Up Form 💪
Pull-Up Technique Tutorial
candidates.description:
Here’s a pull-up technique tutorial to smoothen out your reps.

1. Pull your shoulder blades down your back and hold them in place throughout the pull-up.

2. Use a slightly wider grip, pulling your elbows towards your sides.

3. Aim to pull vertically instead of pulling back, then into the bar.

4. Use the front of your core to form a hollow body shape instead of using your lower back.

This is just one of many pull-up technique options. Give it a go, and let me know how you like it! If you’d like me to cover other types of pull-ups (arched, close grip, archer, wide, high..etc), let me know in the comments below.

candidates.title: The Perfect Pull-Up (FIX THESE!)
candidates.description:
5 Form Tips for the Perfect Pull-Up

1. Shoulders Down and Back: Keep your shoulders down and back at the top of the movement to engage your lats while avoiding excessive involvement of your shoulders and traps.

2. Thumbless Grip for Better Lat Activation: Opt for a thumbless grip to minimize forearm engagement and maximize lat activation, making your pull-ups more efficient.

3. Full-Body Tension: Engage your entire body—including your core, quads, hamstrings, and calves—to prevent energy leaks and maintain a strong, controlled movement.

4. Optimal Grip Width: Use a grip slightly wider than shoulder-width. Avoid going too wide, as this can strain your shoulders and limit your range of motion.

5. Minimize Swinging: Keep your body controlled and minimize swinging to maintain your pull-up strength.

6. Elbow Positioning: Avoid excessive elbow flaring to engage your lats more effectively and maintain proper form.

candidates.title: Do More Pull Ups | How To | US Marine
Pull-Up Variations (KNOW THE DIFFERENCE!)
candidates.description:
Pull-Up Variations – Know the Difference!

✅ Standard Grip Pull-Ups
Targets the lats the most. A balanced back-builder with moderate biceps activation.

✅ Close-Grip Pull-Ups
More biceps and forearm involvement. Lats still work hard, but slightly less than with a standard grip.

✅ Underhand Grip Pull-Ups (Chin-Ups)
Maximizes biceps engagement. Lats are still heavily involved but slightly less dominant than in standard grip pull-ups
